questions.prompt: Which tasks should enter the available-task heap at the current time?

choices.label: All tasks, including those that have not arrived.
choices.feedback: A task may run once it has arrived, including tasks that have been waiting while another task ran.

choices.label: All unprocessed tasks whose arrival time has been reached.
choices.feedback: A task may run once it has arrived, including tasks that have been waiting while another task ran.

choices.label: Only tasks arriving at exactly the current time.
choices.feedback: A task may run once it has arrived, including tasks that have been waiting while another task ran.

questions.prompt: How should an available task be selected?

choices.label: Longest processing time, then smallest original index.
choices.feedback: The CPU’s specified tie-break uses original indices only after comparing processing times.

choices.label: Shortest processing time, then smallest original index.
choices.feedback: The CPU’s specified tie-break uses original indices only after comparing processing times.

choices.label: Earliest arrival time, then largest original index.
choices.feedback: The CPU’s specified tie-break uses original indices only after comparing processing times.

questions.prompt: What should happen when no task is available but future tasks remain?

choices.label: Advance the clock to the next arrival time.
choices.feedback: The CPU must wait while idle. Jumping to the next arrival skips time during which no work is possible.

choices.label: Run the next task before its arrival time.
choices.feedback: The CPU must wait while idle. Jumping to the next arrival skips time during which no work is possible.

choices.label: Finish and ignore the future tasks.
choices.feedback: The CPU must wait while idle. Jumping to the next arrival skips time during which no work is possible.
